additional_info.subject: Case opening remark
additional_info.body:
For Socket 1, several error messages with the information "Internal error" were sent to our backend. After closer investigation, it was determined that some charging processes were showing 0.000 kWh, and on March 15, 2025, two different charging processes from two different cards/customers were even aborted. Currently, the charging point has been in the "Charging is being prepared" state for some time. I've included a small excerpt from the communication log that was sent to our backend in the comments section below. 03/14/2025 6:00 PM
On March 14, 2025, 6:34:30 PM +01:00, the status changed to
"NoError, Preparing," followed by two authorizations of the same RFID tag accepted by the backend on March 14, 2025, 6:34:39 PM +01:00 and
March 14, 2025, 6:34:53 PM +01:00.
On March 14, 2025, 6:35:35 PM +01:00, the message
"InternalError, Faulted" followed, and on March 14, 2025, 6:35:39 PM +01:00, it then changed to
"NoError, Preparing." The same card was authorized again at 18:35:46 +01:00 (backend accepted). At 18:36:00 +01:00, the status changed back to "NoError,
Unavailable."
From 18:36:03 +01:00, the status was again "InternalError, Faulted."
At 18:36:11 +01:00, it changed back to "NoError, Available."
At 18:36:22 +01:00, it changed back to "NoError, Preparing."
At 18:36:26 +01:00, the same card was authorized again, and the backend accepted the authorization. The next status message at 18:37:29 +01:00 was "NoError, Finishing."
Subsequently, "NoError,
SuspendedEVSE" was sent at 18:40:49 +01:00.

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0412989-DC/Si-D/AT-[MP / R6 170001968] Outlet1,Charging Issue ‘Authorization’ CRM:00643001355
additional_info.body:
Hi Lara,
We have analyzed the logs, and below are our findings:
|
In the snapshot below, you can see that when the charging session started on outlet 1, the pilot state changed to B2 (cable connected), and the status notification went to 'Preparing.' However, after that, the pilot state changed to A (cable disconnected), which caused the session to be aborted.
In the snapshot below, when the EV got connected again and the pilot state changed to B2, we encountered an error of 'SLAC failure (no PLC link established).' This indicates that the PLC is unable to establish a connection with the EV due to either a physical connection issue with the DC cable or a communication problem. In this scenario, you should replug the cable into the EV, ensuring it is properly tightened and connected.
In the snapshot below, when the charging session is attempted again, the cable is connected, the status notification goes to 'Preparing,' and authorization is accepted. However, the DC cable gets disconnected from the vehicle, as indicated in the logs, where the pilot state changes from B2 to A.
In the snapshot below, the status notification of the outlet changes to 'Unavailable' due to an 'Error Polling CoAP.' This issue is self-recoverable, and the outlets are temporarily out of order because the internal communication with the SECC was lost for a brief period. Our charger will reconnect to the SECC within 5 seconds. While the SECC is unreachable, an 'Outlet Out of Order' flag will be active and will be cleared once the charger reconnects to the SECC.
In the snapshot below, when the SECC of the outlets reconnects with the charger and the charging session is attempted again, we observed in the logs that the session was aborted due to a communication issue with the EV, which was detected from the EV side. In this case, could you please let us know the EV manufacturer and model you're trying to connect?
It was attempted again on DC Outlet 2, and we observed the same issue with the communication problem from the EV side. Please refer to the snapshot below.
We can conclude that there is no issue on the charger side. Initially, we encountered an issue where the cable got disconnected during the charging session attempt. Then, we observed a SLAC failure, where the DC plug was not connected properly. Finally, we are seeing a communication issue from the EV side.
Please let us know if you have any further queries to discuss. If not, we will proceed with closing this ticket.
Thank you.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Shrey
